## Purpose

This SOP describes field procedures for collecting, filtering, and
preserving environmental DNA (eDNA) samples from surface waters. eDNA
consists of DNA shed into the environment by organisms through skin
cells, mucus, feces, gametes, and decomposing tissue. Detecting eDNA
in water samples allows non-invasive detection of aquatic species
(fish, amphibians, invertebrates, pathogens) without direct
observation or capture [@goldberg2016]. Because eDNA is present at extremely low
concentrations, preventing contamination during field collection is
critical. This SOP covers the field side of the workflow; laboratory
processing (filtration, extraction, inhibition testing) is covered in
[SOP-L700 DNA Extraction](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd)
and future SOP-L315 and SOP-L706.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Collection and preservation of water samples for
  eDNA analysis at all EA Program surface water sites (streams, lakes,
  ponds, wetlands, stormwater basins)
- **Does not apply to:** Soil eDNA or soil microbial sampling (see
  [SOP-F701](SOP-F701-soil-microbial-field-sampling.qmd)); tissue
  biopsy or organism capture for DNA; airborne eDNA sampling; lab-side
  filtration, extraction, and molecular analysis
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling design; ensure permits are in place    |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and preserve eDNA samples per this SOP          |
| New Students      | Complete training (including contamination awareness)
                      before participating in eDNA sampling                |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Wading and sampling near water carry slip, fall, and
  drowning hazards. Work in pairs.
- **Chemical:** DNA preservatives (ethanol, Longmire's buffer) are
  flammable (ethanol) or contain EDTA and SDS (Longmire's). Handle
  with gloves.
- **Biological:** Water may contain pathogens. Wear gloves and avoid
  ingestion.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change between samples and sites)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots
- [ ] Safety glasses (when handling preservatives)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). For
ethanol splashes to eyes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes.


## Equipment and Materials

### Sterile Sampling Supplies

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Sterile sample bottles (1 L or 500 mL, single-use) | Individually wrapped; nalgene or Whirl-Pak |
| Sterile disposable filter funnels (enclosed, 0.45 um PES) | e.g., Nalgene analytical filter units; or Sterivex capsule filters |
| 60 mL sterile syringes (Luer-lock)    | For Sterivex filtration                  |
| Sterile forceps (individually wrapped) | If handling open membrane filters        |
| Molecular-grade ethanol (95--100%)     | For preserving filters; dispense from a dedicated squeeze bottle |
| Longmire's buffer (alternative)        | EDTA/SDS-based preservation buffer       |
| Cooler with ice packs                  | Maintain samples at 4 C during transport |
| Ziplock bags (gallon size)             | For double-bagging preserved filters     |
| DI water (molecular-grade or autoclaved) | For field blanks                      |
| Bleach (10% sodium hypochlorite)       | For decontaminating reusable equipment   |

### Field Documentation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Field notebook (Rite in the Rain)      | For recording sample metadata            |
| Chain of custody forms                 | Per [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd) |
| Permanent marker (Sharpie)            | For labeling bottles and bags            |
| GPS unit or smartphone                 | For recording coordinates per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Camera                                | For photo-documenting site conditions    |

::: {.callout-important}
### Contamination Prevention

eDNA sampling is an ultra-clean procedure. The following rules are
non-negotiable:

- Never reuse sample bottles, filter funnels, or syringes.
- Change gloves between every sample and every site.
- Do not open sample bottles or filter packages until the moment of
  use.
- Keep all sterile supplies in sealed bags until deployment.
- The sampler should not have handled live organisms (fish, amphibians)
  immediately before eDNA sampling. If organism handling occurred,
  change all clothing, boots, and gloves, and use fresh equipment.
:::


## Procedure

### Pre-Field Preparation

1. Assemble individually wrapped sterile bottles, filter units,
   syringes, and forceps in a clean, dedicated eDNA field kit.
2. Prepare Longmire's buffer or aliquot molecular-grade ethanol into
   labeled squeeze bottles.
3. Prepare field blank bottles: fill two sterile 1 L bottles with
   molecular-grade DI water in the lab and seal. These travel with the
   field samples.
4. Prepare equipment blank supplies: one additional sterile bottle for
   collecting a rinse of decontaminated equipment.
5. Pre-label all ziplock bags and sample tags using the ID scheme from
   [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd). Use matrix
   code **EB** for equipment blanks and **FB** for field blanks.

### Site Approach and Sample Collection Order

1. If multiple sites will be sampled in one day, sample the least
   likely occupied site (negative reference) first and the most likely
   occupied site last, to minimize the risk of carry-over
   contamination.
2. At each site, approach the sampling location from downstream and
   collect the eDNA sample before entering the water or disturbing
   sediment.
3. Put on a fresh pair of nitrile gloves.
4. Open the sterile sample bottle just before collection. Do not
   touch the inside of the bottle or cap.

### Water Collection

**Grab sampling (preferred for streams < 1 m depth):**

1. Face upstream. Submerge the open bottle to approximately 15 cm
   below the surface, tilted slightly into the current.
2. Fill the bottle to the line (typically 1 L). Cap immediately.
3. Collect replicate samples if required by the study design (commonly
   3 replicates per site).

**Composite sampling (for larger water bodies or variable habitats):**

1. Collect partial volumes (e.g., 250 mL) from 4--5 locations spanning
   the site (different microhabitats, depths, or transect points).
2. Combine into a single sterile 1 L bottle.

### Field Filtration (If Filtering On-Site)

Field filtration concentrates eDNA onto a filter membrane, improving
preservation and reducing the volume transported.

**Sterivex capsule method:**

1. Attach a sterile 60 mL syringe to the Sterivex filter inlet.
2. Draw water from the sample bottle and push through the filter.
   Repeat until the filter clogs or the target volume is filtered
   (typically 500 mL to 1 L). Record the total volume filtered.
3. Expel remaining water from the capsule.
4. Add 1--2 mL of Longmire's buffer or fill with molecular-grade
   ethanol using a syringe [@renshaw2015]. Cap both ends of the Sterivex.
5. Label the capsule and place in a ziplock bag on ice.

**Open filter funnel method:**

1. Pour the sample through a sterile 0.45 um PES filter unit.
2. When filtration is complete, use sterile forceps to fold the filter
   membrane in half (sample side inward) and place in a labeled
   cryovial or ziplock bag.
3. Add preservative (ethanol or Longmire's buffer) to cover the
   filter. Seal.
4. Place on ice immediately.

### If Not Filtering On-Site

If field filtration is not practical, keep the whole-water sample on
ice (4 C) and filter in the lab within 6 hours of collection.
Exceeding 6 hours significantly increases DNA degradation
[@goldberg2016].

### Field Blanks and Controls

- **Field blank:** At one site per sampling event, open a bottle of
  molecular-grade DI water (prepared in the lab), filter it using the
  same method as the field samples, and preserve the filter. This blank
  detects contamination introduced during field handling.
- **Equipment blank:** If any reusable equipment contacts the sample
  (e.g., a pump), collect a rinse of the decontaminated equipment as
  a blank.
- Process blanks alongside field samples through the entire lab
  workflow.

### Decontamination Between Sites

1. Spray or soak all reusable equipment (boots, waders, sampling
   poles) with 10% bleach solution for at least 1 minute.
2. Rinse with clean water.
3. Change gloves.
4. eDNA-specific single-use items (bottles, filters, syringes) are
   discarded after each sample and do not require decontamination.

See [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd) for general
decontamination procedures.


## Sample Transport and Storage

1. Keep all samples and preserved filters on ice (4 C) during
   transport.
2. Deliver to the lab the same day. If overnight storage is
   unavoidable, store at -20 C.
3. For long-term storage (> 1 week before extraction), store preserved
   filters at -20 C or -80 C.
4. Complete the chain of custody form per
   [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd).


## Quality Control

- Minimum 1 field blank per sampling event; 1 equipment blank if
  reusable equipment is used.
- Collect 3 replicate samples per site unless the study design
  specifies otherwise.
- Record the total volume filtered for each sample (required for
  calculating eDNA concentration).
- Any field blank that tests positive for target DNA invalidates the
  samples from that event unless the concentration is below a
  pre-established threshold. Consult the PI.
- Log all glove changes, bottle openings, and deviations in the field
  notebook.

## Training Record

Before collecting eDNA samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd), and
   [SOP-L700](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate proper sterile technique (glove changes, bottle
   handling, filter preservation) during a supervised practice session
3. Successfully process a field blank with a negative result
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
